newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Imelda Marcos appeals $887 mln tax judgment.
newsitem.headline: Imelda Marcos appeals $887 mln tax judgment.

text.p: Former Philippine first lady Imelda Marcos asked the Supreme Court on Monday to revoke an $887 million tax judgment against her family, saying the state had seized all their possessions and there was nothing left to tax.

The widow of late president Ferdinand Marcos personally went to the court to file her appeal against its June 5 ruling, which upheld a lower court's order to seize and sell 11 plots of family land to cover unpaid estate taxes.
"They (the government) took even our ancestral homes. All our personal belongings were taken away from us...There is nothing left. What is there to tax?" she told reporters.

The government has accused the Marcoses of stealing up to $5 billion from the economy during their 20-year rule and seized Marcos-linked assets after the former president was overthrown in a 1986 popular revolt.
Dozens of cases are now pending in court to determine their ownership. Ferdinand Marcos died in exile in Hawaii in 1989.
Marcos, now a congresswoman, called the tax assessment "whimsical (and) dictatorial" and said it violated a government ruling excluding state-sequestered property from assessments.
The tax judgment is the latest blow for the once powerful family.

In 1993, Mrs Marcos was convicted of corruption by a Manila court and sentenced to 18 years in jail. The next year, her son, Ferdinand Jr, was sentenced to nine years behind bars for tax evasion. Both are out on bail while the cases are on appeal.
A Hawaiian jury in 1994 also ordered the Marcos estate to pay $1.2 billion in damages to thousands of Filipinos who suffered human rights abuses during the Marcos regime.

Another jury in Hawaii in 1996 awarded $22 billion in damages to representatives of a Filipino locksmith who had accused the late president of stealing his statue of Buddha, supposedly made of gold. The decisions are also on appeal.
